figure_discussions.caption: TEG Dehydration: Effect of Circulation Rate on Water Content. CPA SimpleTEGAbsorber with explicit fixed-inventory energy reconstruction; 99.5 weight percent lean TEG, five stages and 70 percent stage efficiency.
figure_discussions.title: TEG Dehydration: Effect of Circulation Rate on Water Content
figure_discussions.observation: Dry-gas water decreases from 36.596 ppmv at 500 kg/hr circulation to a sampled minimum of 18.177 ppmv at 4181.8 kg/hr, then rises slightly to 18.195 ppmv at 5000 kg/hr. All reconstructed cases retain explicit material and energy checks.
figure_discussions.mechanism: The CPA/Kremser approximation is rerun at each circulation rate, then a common outlet temperature closes the adiabatic energy balance while preserving its predicted component inventories. The 40 °C lean solvent is warmer than the 25 °C gas, so additional circulation combines increased absorption with sensible heating.
figure_discussions.implication: The shallow minimum shows that more solvent does not guarantee a monotonically lower water content; the native contacting approximation is not a rigorous multistage energy model.
figure_discussions.recommendation: Use the minimum as a screening observation, verify lean-solvent purity and thermal conditions, and calibrate contacting performance before selecting a field circulation rate.
